headline: High: dexter’s autonomous API/file activity can leak financial data and amplify bad outputs; prompt-injection risk is limited by the pair’s weak direct coupling.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented between awesome-cli-apps and dexter, so direct injection is not evidenced. However, dexter has autonomous execution and file/API surfaces, so if the pair is manually bridged through copied content or a shared workspace, attacker-controlled text from one could influence the other. The pathway is plausible but not default.
conditions: IF the operator copies agent_a output into agent_b prompts or scratchpad files
IF both agents are pointed at the same shared directory or clipboard bridge
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate workspaces
Disable copy-paste bridging during runs
Add a human review step before passing text between agents
Use provenance labels on any transferred content
requires-engineering: add channel isolation or signed message passing

B_data_leakage.rationale: dexter touches financial and market data and writes to .dexter/scratchpad/, while awesome-cli-apps has broad network egress. If they share a workspace or credentials, dexter’s sensitive outputs can be exposed and then transmitted by the other agent. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default-style operator setups, though not directly proven.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b share a filesystem or synced workspace
IF agent_b writes sensitive market or financial data into .dexter/scratchpad/
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Restrict network egress for the content-writing agent
Rotate any shared API keys before co-running
Review scratchpad contents before reuse
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress, and dexter also supports multiple instances plus autonomous execution. That creates overlapping write-like pressure on shared external resources such as APIs or shared files if the operator co-locates them. The profiles do not show a locking mechanism, so conflict is plausible rather than blocked.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same external API account or shared workspace
IF multiple dexter instances run concurrently without an orchestrator lock
mitigations: Run only one writer at a time
Assign separate API keys per agent
Avoid shared mutable directories
Add a manual lock file before writes
requires-engineering: implement resource-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-cli-apps is a content-writing agent, so its outputs can be treated as authoritative text by dexter’s autonomous workflow if the operator chains them. dexter’s API-driven execution increases the chance that unverified content becomes downstream action or analysis. The pair lacks any documented verification barrier, so cascading error is a realistic default-path concern.
conditions: IF agent_a output is fed into agent_b without a verification step
IF agent_b is allowed to act autonomously on generated text
mitigations: Insert a human verification step between agents
Require citations for any factual claims before reuse
Limit dexter to read-only analysis mode
Log and diff all transferred outputs
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking gates

E_compliance.rationale: dexter explicitly touches financial and market data and uses third-party APIs, while awesome-cli-apps has broad network egress and no documented residency or retention controls. That combination can create compliance mismatch around data handling and logging, especially if regulated financial data is routed through external services. The other agent is not cited for a specific residency claim because none is documented.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is processed through dexter’s external APIs
IF logs or scratchpad contents are retained beyond the operator’s policy
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to external APIs
Review retention settings for all connected services
Purge scratchpad files after each run
Confirm vendor DPAs before use
requires-engineering: add residency and retention enforcement
